plan.title: Liver treated-vs-control DE with n=3 confidence assessment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a small, clean design: Salmon-derived gene-level integer counts for 12,000 genes across 6 human liver samples, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. With n=3 per group there are only 4 residual degrees of freedom, so the plan must both produce a defensible DE list and quantify how much of it is stable. Step T1S1 loads and matches counts to metadata, filters near-zero genes, runs DESeq2 (negative binomial GLM with empirical-Bayes dispersion shrinkage, appropriate for tiny n), applies BH FDR, and produces diagnostics (PCA, sample distances, dispersion fit) to confirm the samples are exchangeable within group. Step T1S2 interrogates confidence directly: leave-one-out re-runs of the DE model to measure how many calls survive dropping each sample, concordance with an independent count-based method (edgeR, robust GLM with quasi-likelihood F-tests), and shrunk (apeglm) vs raw log2FC comparison, since with n=3 raw LFCs are wildly variable and false positives concentrate among low-count genes. Step T1S3 tests whether the treated-vs-control signal organizes into biology at all by running pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea) on the signed test statistic against the provisioned WikiPathways human gene sets — a rank-based check that is more robust to the weak per-gene power than an FDR-cutoff overlap test. No batch, pairing, or covariate terms exist to model; the design formula is ~condition.
